fields.name: approval_limit_amount
fields.label: Amount
fields.sourceQuote: You can enter 0 in the Amount field.
fields.notes: BRANCH B, right side of the window; the second control in the unnamed 'Approval Limit area'. NEVER the same field record as field.workflows.authorized-approver-approval-limit (labeled 'Approval Limit', from authorized-approver-list-a9522ec8.md, Workflows-path only) — this window's own control is explicitly labeled 'the Amount field', a different label on a different surface writing the same underlying per-approver value (three-setter verdict, see step-4-assign-the-proper-rights-to-users-86389a18.md). VALUE SEMANTICS: 0 = 'This puts the approver into the authorized approver workflow but will prevent that approver from having final authority to approve the invoice (cannot limit-approve)... since the Limit Approved status is not changed, the invoice moves to the next authorized approver or processor' (fcfd570c). NULL/blank = unlimited, stated here as ONE act: 'For an unlimited approval amount, leave blank (null).' (8b167b96) — surface-agnostic corroboration in setting-an-unlimited-approval-amount-9d98b489.md: 'a limit amount of null will result in an unlimited approval/no limit approval amount.' CONTRADICTION 3: Workflows/a9522ec8 requires a TWO-ACT unlimited recipe ('set to no approval limit currency, and leave the approval limit amount blank'); this window and 9d98b489 each state only ONE act. Whether the currency must ALSO be cleared here is UNDETERMINED BY THE DOCUMENTATION — do not import the Workflows two-act recipe onto this window. Value domain 'Numeric' / 'Specified in the approval limit currency' is documented only on employee-import-e28f2294.md (value-domain citation only, not a page source).

fields.name: cost_object_approval_level
fields.label: Level
fields.sourceQuote: For level-based cost object approval, select a level.
fields.notes: BRANCH B, right side of the window, CONTESTED. 8b167b96 documents this control on the window; filter-authorized-approvers-by-workflow-approval-step-aae69350.md states the flat opposite: 'Levels cannot be added to approvers via User Administration.' and 'The levels can be added to users via the Employee Import or the Authorized Approver list (Administration > Invoice > Workflows > Authorized Approver tab).' Both grep -F verify; see contradictions[] — NOT RESOLVED, recorded as a hypothesis only. HYPOTHESIS (not adopted as fact): these are two DIFFERENT VALUES sharing one label. aae69350's 'Level' is the authorized-approver workflow-step FILTER (employee import record TYPE 720 per step-2-assign-the-level-to-the-approver-d8bf669c.md — 'authorized approvers may be assigned to levels via record type 720 in the employee import' — feeding the Authorized Approver Hierarchy), while 8b167b96's 'Level' is the level-based COST OBJECT APPROVAL level (employee import record SET 710 per employee-import-e28f2294.md, feeding a separately-named Cost Object Approver Hierarchy per step-1-define-the-cost-object-approver-hierarchy-6e7b7dc6.md). Given this distinction, name it cost_object_approval_level and NEVER present it as a sibling of the built field.workflows.authorized-approver-level. STRUCTURAL CONTEXT for the contradiction: 8b167b96 belongs to the Cost Object Approval guide thread (gates on 'the Cost Object Approver feature'; rev-history root cost-object-approval-8b3d1e0f.md; Step 4 sibling step-4-assign-the-proper-rights-to-users-82481079.md; Configuration sibling configuration-8b3cce3f.md), a materially different chapter than fcfd570c's Authorized Approvers guide thread — offered as a hypothesis for why the two attestations diverge, not as a resolution. PRECEDENCE RULE (see dependencyCandidates): if BOTH the Approval Limit area and this Level field are completed, 'Concur Invoice will use the one that applies to your configuration and ignore the other' (8b167b96) — the cost object configuration (limit vs level, per level-based-approvals-and-limit-based-approvals-b335cf33.md) decides which is authoritative.

contradictions.topic: Whether a Level control exists on the Authorized Approval Limits window at all

readings.summary: 8b167b96 documents a Level control directly in the Authorized Approval Limits window, for level-based cost object approval.
readings.sourceQuote: For level-based cost object approval, select a level.

readings.summary: filter-authorized-approvers-by-workflow-approval-step-aae69350.md states flatly that levels cannot be added to approvers via User Administration at all, and names only the Employee Import and the Workflows Authorized Approver list as the places levels can be added.
readings.sourceQuote: Levels cannot be added to approvers via User Administration.

contradictions.consequenceForWriter: Do not assume this control is reachable through User Administration until it is confirmed against a live instance. If it is missing at runtime, fall back to the Employee Import (record type 720) or the Authorized Approver List on Workflows (Administration > Invoice > Workflows > Authorized Approver tab) to set an approver's level. Treat the two Level values as potentially DIFFERENT underlying fields (see hypothesis in notes) rather than one shared control, so do not write cost_object_approval_level and field.workflows.authorized-approver-level as interchangeable targets for the same driver action.
contradictions.notes: HYPOTHESIS, not adopted as resolved: the two sentences may not actually be describing the same field. aae69350's 'Level' is the authorized-approver workflow-step filter, fed by employee import record TYPE 720 (per step-2-assign-the-level-to-the-approver-d8bf669c.md) into the Authorized Approver Hierarchy. 8b167b96's 'Level' is the level-based cost object approval level, fed by employee import record SET 710 (per employee-import-e28f2294.md) into a separately-named Cost Object Approver Hierarchy. Structurally, 8b167b96 and aae69350 also come from different guide chapters (Cost Object Approval vs Workflows/Authorized Approvers), which may explain the divergence without either file being simply wrong.

readings.sourceQuote: If the Authorized Approver feature is activated and the company's Authorized Approver hierarchy has at least one level (in addition to Global), then the Authorized Approval Limits link appears in the Expense and Invoices Setting section in Administration > Company > Company Admin > User Administration.

readings.summary: 8b167b96 (Cost Object Approval guide thread) leads with the Cost Object Approver feature as the gate, then separately restates the Authorized-Approver/hierarchy condition in its own Note — so this file's own text requires BOTH named features together, unlike fcfd570c which names only one.
readings.sourceQuote: When the Cost Object Approver feature is activated, the Authorized Approval Limits link appears in the Expense and Invoices Settings section in User Administration.

contradictions.consequenceForWriter: Before relying on this link's visibility as a precondition, check BOTH the Authorized Approver feature and the Cost Object Approver feature (plus the non-Global hierarchy level) rather than assuming either one alone is sufficient — the two guide threads describe the same link from two different chapters' vantage points and neither states outright that both features are simultaneously required, but 8b167b96 internally names both.
contradictions.notes: HYPOTHESIS for the cause: chapter provenance. fcfd570c is in the Authorized Approvers guide (rev-history root authorized-approvers-8b3c26cc.md; Step 4 sibling step-4-assign-the-proper-rights-to-users-86389a18.md); 8b167b96 is in the Cost Object Approval guide (rev-history root cost-object-approval-8b3d1e0f.md; Step 4 sibling step-4-assign-the-proper-rights-to-users-82481079.md; Configuration sibling configuration-8b3cce3f.md), each naming its own chapter's feature as the headline gate. grep -rlF 'Cost Object Approver feature' across both guide directories returns only 8b167b96 and configuration-8b3cce3f.md.

contradictions.topic: The unlimited-approval-amount recipe: does clearing the currency matter, in addition to leaving the amount blank

readings.summary: On this window, 8b167b96 states a ONE-act recipe: leave the amount blank/null. No mention of the currency.
readings.sourceQuote: For an unlimited approval amount, leave blank (null).

readings.summary: The Workflows sibling surface (Authorized Approver List, a9522ec8.md — boundary evidence only, not a source for this page's fields) requires a TWO-act recipe: clear the currency AND leave the amount blank.
readings.sourceQuote: set to no approval limit currency, and leave the approval limit amount blank

contradictions.consequenceForWriter: Do not import the Workflows two-act recipe onto this window. Whether the currency must also be cleared here is UNDETERMINED by the documentation; a driver automating 'set unlimited' on this window should leave the amount blank per 8b167b96/9d98b489, and only additionally clear the currency if a live-instance check shows the amount alone is insufficient.
contradictions.notes: setting-an-unlimited-approval-amount-9d98b489.md is surface-agnostic and also states only one act ('a limit amount of null will result in an unlimited approval/no limit approval amount'), matching this window's single-act recipe rather than the Workflows two-act one. No third file breaks the tie.
